evals.title: File Naming Standard Violation
evals.prompt: Review this Dart file path and identify naming standard violations. The file is located at: lib/src/domain/entities/UserEntity.dart - Does it follow snake_case conventions?
evals.expected_output: The file violates Dart naming standards. Files must use snake_case (e.g., user_entity.dart), not PascalCase. Expected: lib/src/domain/entities/user_entity.dart

assertions.text: The assistant identifies that 'UserEntity.dart' violates snake_case naming convention
The assistant provides the correct file name 'user_entity.dart'

evals.title: Class Naming Conventions in Clean Architecture
evals.expected_output: Violations: 'user_repository' should be 'UserRepository' (PascalCase). 'user_model' should be 'UserModel' (PascalCase). Correct naming: UserRepository (interface), GetUserUseCase, UserModel, UserRepositoryImpl.

assertions.text: Identifies all three naming violations: 'user_repository', 'user_model', and incorrect usage patterns
Provides correct naming for all three classes: UserRepository, UserModel, UserRepositoryImpl
Explains PascalCase rule for all class types

evals.title: const vs final vs late Decision (Edge Case)
evals.expected_output: Line 2 is problematic: 'late final user = ...' tries to assign in late declaration (should be 'final user = await fetchUser()' or 'late final user;' + separate initialization). Line 4: 'const var config = ...' won't work because 'var' is dynamic and config is runtime-computed; use 'final' instead.

assertions.text: Identifies that 'late final user = fetchUser()' is problematic (late cannot be initialized immediately)
Identifies that 'const var config = loadConfig()' is wrong (config is runtime, not compile-time)
Provides correct alternatives: 'final user = await fetchUser()' and 'final config = loadConfig()'

evals.title: Import Organization Correctness
evals.prompt: Reorder these imports according to the coding standards. Identify which organization is correct:\nA) import 'package:flutter/material.dart'; import 'dart:async'; import '../entities/user.dart'; import 'package:equatable/equatable.dart';\nB) import 'dart:async'; import 'package:flutter/material.dart'; import 'package:equatable/equatable.dart'; import '../entities/user.dart';
evals.expected_output: Option B is correct. Import order: (1) dart imports, (2) flutter imports, (3) packages, (4) relative imports. Option A violates this by placing flutter before dart and relative after packages.

assertions.text: Correctly identifies Option B as the correct import organization
Explains the ordering rule: dart → flutter → packages → relative

evals.title: Logging Standards: print vs log
evals.expected_output: All print() and debugPrint() calls violate standards. They should use the log interface: log.debug(), log.info(), log.error(). Replace: 'print(...)' → 'log.info(...)', 'debugPrint(...)' → 'log.debug(...)'. Never use print() in production code.

assertions.text: Identifies all three instances of print()/debugPrint() violations (3 occurrences minimum)
Recommends using log.info(), log.debug(), log.error() replacements
States that print() should never be used in production code

evals.title: Documentation for Public API Methods

assertions.text: Identifies missing /// documentation comment for public method
Recommends documentation covering: method purpose, return type, exceptions thrown
Provides a complete example documentation template with ///

evals.title: Trailing Commas in Multi-line Calls

assertions.text: Identifies the missing trailing comma after 'includeDetails: true'
Explains that trailing commas enable auto-format and improve diffs

evals.title: Null Safety Violations
evals.expected_output: Violations: (1) 'User user = null;' should be 'User? user;' (nullable type). (2) 'user.name!' is unsafe unwrap without null check. (3) Line 8 checks 'user != null' but doesn't narrow type for safe access. Fix: Make user nullable, check before use, or use 'user?.name ?? defaultValue'.

assertions.text: Identifies that 'User user = null;' should use explicit nullable type 'User?'
Flags 'user.name!' as unsafe unwrap without null narrowing
Identifies that null check does not narrow the type for safe access in the current code

evals.title: Custom Exceptions vs Generic Exception
evals.expected_output: Using generic 'Exception' violates standards. Should create custom exceptions: 'class FetchDataException extends AppException { FetchDataException(String msg) : super(msg); }' then throw 'FetchDataException('Failed to fetch data')'.

assertions.text: Identifies that throwing generic 'Exception' violates standards
Recommends creating a custom exception class (e.g., FetchDataException)
Provides implementation example of custom AppException hierarchy

evals.title: Equatable Implementation for Entity Comparison
evals.expected_output: UserEntity must extend Equatable and override 'props'. Currently, u1 == u2 will be false (different object references). Fix: 'class UserEntity extends Equatable { ... @override List<Object> get props => [id, name]; }' to enable proper equality comparison.

assertions.text: Identifies that UserEntity does not extend Equatable (comparison will fail)
Recommends extending Equatable and overriding 'props'
Provides complete code fix showing 'extends Equatable' and '@override List<Object> get props'

evals.title: Boolean Variable Naming Conventions
evals.expected_output: Violations: 'loading' should be 'isLoading', 'errorState' should be 'hasError' or 'isError', 'active' should be 'isActive'. The 'userCanDelete' naming is acceptable but 'canDelete' is cleaner. Correct: isAuthenticated, hasNotifications follow the is/has/can prefix rule.

assertions.text: Identifies 'loading' as a violation — should use 'isLoading' prefix
Identifies 'active' as a violation — should be 'isActive'
Identifies 'errorState' as a violation — should be 'isError' or 'hasError'
Correctly confirms 'isAuthenticated' and 'hasNotifications' as valid

evals.title: Private Member Naming with Underscore Prefix
evals.expected_output: Violations: 'remoteSource' and 'localSource' are intended to be private but lack the underscore prefix — should be '_remoteSource' and '_localSource'. '_repo' is named correctly but should be 'late final' for DI-injected fields. 'formatAmount' is public (no underscore) — if it should be private, rename to '_formatAmount'.

assertions.text: Identifies 'remoteSource' as missing the underscore prefix for private visibility
Identifies 'localSource' as missing the underscore prefix for private visibility
Mentions that 'late final' should be used for injected fields set exactly once

evals.title: String Interpolation vs Concatenation
evals.expected_output: Lines 1 and 2 violate the 'prefer_interpolation_to_compose_strings' rule — use string interpolation instead. Correct: 'Hello, ${user.name}!' and '$baseUrl/users/$userId/profile'. Lines 3 and 4 are correct: simple variable uses '$var', expression uses '${expression}'.

assertions.text: Identifies the first string concatenation (greeting) as a violation
Identifies the second string concatenation (url) as a violation
Provides correct interpolation alternatives for both violations
Confirms lines 3 and 4 are correct (simple $var and ${expression} patterns)

evals.title: Enum and Typedef Naming Conventions
evals.expected_output: Violations: 'payment_status' should be 'PaymentStatus' (PascalCase enum). Enum values should be camelCase: 'pending', 'completed', 'failed' (not SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE). 'onUserLoaded' typedef should be 'OnUserLoaded' (PascalCase). 'cache_strategy' mixin should be 'CacheStrategy' (PascalCase). Correct: 'ApiStatus' and enum values 'loading/success/error', 'JsonMap' typedef.

assertions.text: Identifies 'payment_status' as a violation — should be 'PaymentStatus' (PascalCase)
Identifies SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE enum values (PENDING, COMPLETED, FAILED) as violations — should be camelCase
Identifies 'onUserLoaded' typedef as a violation — should be 'OnUserLoaded' (PascalCase)
Identifies 'cache_strategy' mixin as a violation — should be 'CacheStrategy' (PascalCase)

evals.title: Choosing the Right Linting Package
evals.prompt: I'm starting a new open-source Flutter package that I plan to publish on pub.dev. It's a small utilities library with a few helper functions. Which linting package should I use in analysis_options.yaml and why?
evals.expected_output: For an open-source pub.dev package, 'lint' or 'flutter_lints' is typically appropriate — they have medium strictness suitable for libraries consumed by others with different coding styles. 'very_good_analysis' can be too strict for open-source libraries (contributors may struggle). Provides a sample analysis_options.yaml snippet.

assertions.text: Recommends 'lint' or 'flutter_lints' for an open-source package (NOT very_good_analysis as the primary recommendation)
Explains the reasoning: open-source packages should be contributor-friendly with moderate strictness
Provides a sample analysis_options.yaml with the recommended include directive
